source: NCERT Class XI, Political Theory, Ch. 1 (Political Theory: An Introduction).

sections.heading: 1. What is Politics?
points: **Politics** is not only about government and elections; it arises wherever people negotiate, cooperate and settle disputes over **collective life and public affairs**.
Politics is the activity through which people make, preserve and amend the general rules under which they live.
It is a **public activity** involving both conflict and cooperation.

sections.heading: 2. What is Political Theory?
points: **Political theory** systematically thinks about **political ideas** — freedom, equality, justice, rights, democracy, citizenship.
It examines the meaning of these concepts, clarifies them, and evaluates existing political arrangements.
Great thinkers (Plato, Aristotle, Gandhi, Ambedkar, Rousseau, Marx) contributed to political theory.

sections.heading: 3. Why Study Political Theory?
points: It helps us **understand and evaluate** our rights, duties and institutions.
It equips citizens to **reason and debate** about public issues responsibly.
As technology and society change (e.g. internet, privacy), new questions arise that political theory helps address.
It clarifies confusing or contested ideas (e.g. 'freedom', 'equality').

sections.heading: 4. High-Yield One-Liners (Last-Minute Recall)
points: Politics = activity of making, preserving and amending general rules of collective life.
Political theory = systematic reflection on political ideas (freedom, equality, justice, rights).
It involves both conflict and cooperation (public activity).
Thinkers: Plato, Aristotle, Rousseau, Marx, Gandhi, Ambedkar.
Political theory helps citizens reason about rights, duties and institutions.

sections.heading: 5. Common Traps (Watch Out)
points: **Politics is not limited to government/elections** — it is present in all collective life.
Political theory **clarifies and evaluates** ideas (it is normative, not just descriptive).
Studying political theory makes us **better, more reasoning citizens**.
